examGuide.title: Mental model and derivation
examGuide.body:
Circuit switching reserves resources, while packet switching statistically shares them. Store-and-forward transmits a packet only after receiving it completely, unless another forwarding model is specified. A virtual circuit uses established path state but still carries packets. Pipeline multiple packets across links rather than summing full-file delays on every link. Setup costs and per-packet headers can change comparisons between methods.

**Key relationship:** Store-and-forward one packet over k equal links: k·L/R, ignoring other delays

examGuide.title: A repeatable solving procedure
examGuide.body:
1. Specify store-and-forward or cut-through.
2. Separate setup, serialization and propagation.
3. Pipeline successive packets across links.

examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: Packet store-and-forward begins forwarding after a full packet arrives, but links can pipeline consecutive packets. For N equal packets over k equal-rate links, negligible propagation gives (N+k−1) packet-transmission times. Circuit switching may have setup and reserved rate; do not substitute one model for the other.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
Ten 1000-bit packets cross three 1 Mbps links with store-and-forward and negligible other delays. What total time is required in milliseconds?

**Answer: 12.** One packet takes 1 ms per link. The first reaches the destination after 3 ms; nine more arrive one per millisecond. Total=(10+3−1)·1=12 ms.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
Sending one whole file as a single store-and-forward unit has a different fill cost from dividing it into packets.

A virtual circuit is not automatically a reserved-bandwidth circuit.

examGuide.title: Worked question patterns
examGuide.body:
#### Pattern 1 · MCQ

Store-and-forward means a node generally forwards a packet after:

- **A.** Receiving only its first bit
- **B.** Receiving the whole packet
- **C.** Every file completes
- **D.** A circuit is always reserved

**Answer: B.** Complete reception precedes outgoing serialization under the standard store-and-forward model.

#### Pattern 2 · MSQ

Choose true statements.

- **A.** Circuit switching may reserve capacity
- **B.** Packet switching can share links statistically
- **C.** Virtual circuits are necessarily physical dedicated wires
- **D.** Store-and-forward can pipeline different packets

**Answer: A, B, D.** Virtual circuits maintain logical path state; they need not dedicate a physical wire.

#### Pattern 3 · NAT

Three equal links each need 2 ms to serialize one packet, zero propagation. Time for one store-and-forward packet in ms?



**Answer: 6.** The packet is serialized sequentially on three links: 3·2=6 ms. Multiple packets could then overlap.

examGuide.title: Work through the supplied PYQs
examGuide.body:
#### GATE 2024 CS1 · Q36 · MCQ

[Open the original question and try it](/#/lesson/network-switching?tab=practice)

**What is tested:** Circuit, packet and virtual-circuit switching. Refer to the original image for complete givens and diagrams.

1. There are 10⁶/10³=1000 chunks. Each chunk takes 1000×8/10⁶=0.008 s per link.
2. The router pipelines store-and-forward packets: the first reaches R after 2×0.008 s and each later packet arrives 0.008 s after its predecessor.
3. Total=(1000+2−1)×0.008=**8.008 s, B**.
